notes.s: The day resets at midnight whether or not anything got better.
notes.t: A vocal-line song from Map of the Soul: 7 about an ordinary bad day, not a dramatic one: your body is heavy, everyone else looks like they are coping, and you cannot work out which part was your fault. Instead of resolving it, the song waits for the clock. The second hand and the minute hand stack up at twelve, the day is legally over, and that is the entire comfort on offer. ARMY took it up as the quiet counterweight to the album's louder tracks, and the English line about being happy is sung as a promise to yourself rather than a prediction.
k: -잖아 hands something to the listener as already shared, so this opens in the middle of a conversation rather than introducing a topic. A learner can lift this straight into speech: 피곤하잖아, you're tired, you know.
초침 is the second hand and 분침 the minute hand, literally second-needle and minute-needle. At midnight they line up on top of each other, and the title is that overlap rather than a time of night.
내 맘 같은 게 뭐 하나 없어

내 맘 같다 means to be the way my heart would have it. Negated with 뭐 하나 없어, not one thing, it is the standard way to say nothing is cooperating, and much less self-pitying in Korean than a word-for-word English version sounds.
Wishes get cut off after -기를 and the verb 바라다, to hope, is left unsaid. The effect is prayer rather than statement, which is why the preceding line has hands pressed together.

vocab.note: Used of moods and atmospheres as well as objects
Standard word for brutal competition, as in 치열한 경쟁
발걸음이 떨어지지 않다, the step won't come off, means you can't bring yourself to go
숨을 참다 hold your breath, 눈물을 참다 hold back tears
숨을 쉬다 is to breathe; the identical 쉬다 meaning to rest is a separate word, context decides
표정을 짓다, to build an expression, is the normal verb pairing
